title: Left Front Wheel Speed Sensor Circuit
shortDescription: ABS wheel speed sensor fault: left front wheel speed sensor circuit.
fullDescription: The ABS/ESP module compares wheel speed sensor inputs to detect slip and modulate brake pressure. Left Front Wheel Speed Sensor Circuit indicates a sensor circuit problem that disables ABS, traction control, and stability control until repaired.
safetyImpact: ABS, traction, and stability control are disabled. Braking distance increases on slippery surfaces and the vehicle has no electronic stability assistance.

causes.cause: Damaged or contaminated wheel speed sensor
Damaged tone ring (broken teeth, rust pack)

symptoms: Speedometer may flicker or read zero (some platforms)

fixSteps.title: Scan ABS/ESP Module
fixSteps.instruction: Connect a scan tool capable of ABS/chassis communication. Read freeze frame, identify which wheel or sensor is reported, and view live wheel speed PIDs while rotating wheels.

fixSteps.title: Inspect wheel speed sensor and tone ring
fixSteps.instruction: Visually inspect the wheel speed sensor and tone ring, harness, and connector for damage, contamination, missing teeth on the tone ring, or corrosion. Clean and reseat connector.

fixSteps.title: Measure Sensor Output
fixSteps.instruction: Backprobe the sensor connector. With the wheel raised, rotate by hand and measure AC voltage (passive) or square-wave signal (active) with a multimeter or oscilloscope.

fixSteps.title: Replace wheel speed sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the wheel speed sensor with an OEM unit. Torque to spec. Clear codes and verify ABS/ESP self-test passes during a road test.

faq.q: Is it safe to drive with the ABS light on?
faq.a: The base hydraulic brakes still work, but ABS and ESP are off. Drive cautiously and avoid slippery conditions until repaired.

faq.q: Will the code reset itself?
faq.a: The lamp usually clears after a few drive cycles once the fault is repaired. A scan tool clear is faster.

faq.q: Could a wheel bearing cause this?
faq.a: Yes — excessive bearing play moves the tone ring out of the sensor's air gap and produces intermittent or low-amplitude signals.

fixSteps.instruction: Backprobe the sensor connector. With the wheel raised, rotate by hand and measure AC voltage (passive) or square-wave signal (active) with a multimeter or oscilloscope.

fixSteps.title: Replace wheel speed sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the wheel speed sensor with an OEM unit. Torque to spec. Clear codes and verify ABS/ESP self-test passes during a road test.

faq.q: Is it safe to drive with the ABS light on?
faq.a: The base hydraulic brakes still work, but ABS and ESP are off. Drive cautiously and avoid slippery conditions until repaired.

faq.q: Will the code reset itself?
faq.a: The lamp usually clears after a few drive cycles once the fault is repaired. A scan tool clear is faster.

faq.q: Could a wheel bearing cause this?
faq.a: Yes — excessive bearing play moves the tone ring out of the sensor's air gap and produces intermittent or low-amplitude signals.

title: Wheel Speed Sensor Frequency Error
shortDescription: The wheel speed sensor frequency does not match the expected pattern.
fullDescription: The ABS module has detected that the wheel speed signal has missing or extra pulses, indicating a damaged tone ring, a sensor with debris on the tip, or a sensor air gap that is out of specification.
safetyImpact: ABS and stability control are disabled until the cause is corrected.

causes.cause: Metal debris stuck to magnetic sensor tip

symptoms: Brief unintended ABS activation at low speed

fixSteps.title: Scan ABS/ESP Module
fixSteps.instruction: Connect a scan tool capable of ABS/chassis communication. Read freeze frame, identify which wheel or sensor is reported, and view live wheel speed PIDs while rotating wheels.

fixSteps.title: Inspect sensor tip and tone ring
fixSteps.instruction: Visually inspect the sensor tip and tone ring, harness, and connector for damage, contamination, missing teeth on the tone ring, or corrosion. Clean and reseat connector.

fixSteps.title: Measure Sensor Output
fixSteps.instruction: Backprobe the sensor connector. With the wheel raised, rotate by hand and measure AC voltage (passive) or square-wave signal (active) with a multimeter or oscilloscope.

fixSteps.title: Replace wheel speed sensor or tone ring
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the wheel speed sensor or tone ring with an OEM unit. Torque to spec. Clear codes and verify ABS/ESP self-test passes during a road test.

faq.q: Why does ABS engage at low speed for no reason?
faq.a: A skipped tooth on the tone ring tells the module a wheel briefly stopped, which it interprets as lockup.

faq.q: Can I clean the sensor?
faq.a: Yes — many cases are resolved by removing the sensor and wiping ferrous debris off the magnetic tip.

faq.q: Are tone rings sold separately?
faq.a: Some are replaceable; on many vehicles the tone ring is integral to the wheel bearing or CV joint.

title: Steering Wheel Torque Sensor Circuit
shortDescription: Electric power steering / steering torque sensor fault: steering wheel torque sensor circuit.
fullDescription: The steering control module monitors torque, angle, motor current, and module health to provide variable assist. Steering Wheel Torque Sensor Circuit disables or reduces power steering assist until cleared and may also disable lane-keep assist.
safetyImpact: Loss of power steering assist requires significantly more effort, especially at low speed. Lane-keep and parking assist are typically disabled.

causes.cause: Failed torque or angle sensor inside steering column
Loss of CAN communication to EPS module
Steering angle sensor not calibrated after alignment

fixSteps.title: Scan ABS/ESP Module
fixSteps.instruction: Connect a scan tool capable of ABS/chassis communication. Read freeze frame, identify which wheel or sensor is reported, and view live wheel speed PIDs while rotating wheels.

fixSteps.title: Check Battery and Charging Voltage
fixSteps.instruction: EPS faults are often triggered by marginal voltage. Load test the battery and verify alternator output is within spec under EPS load.

fixSteps.title: Perform Steering Angle Calibration
fixSteps.instruction: After any alignment, suspension, or EPS work, run the OEM steering angle sensor calibration. Some vehicles auto-calibrate after a low-speed drive cycle.

fixSteps.title: Replace Faulty EPS Component
fixSteps.instruction: Based on data, replace the steering rack/column assembly or EPS controller. Always re-calibrate and confirm no related codes return.

faq.q: Is it safe to drive without power steering?
faq.a: Possible at higher speed but very heavy at parking speed. Avoid if you have any physical limitation that makes manual steering unsafe.

faq.q: Why does battery voltage matter for EPS?
faq.a: EPS motors draw 60–100 amps under load; voltage sag below ~10.5V triggers protection codes.

faq.q: Does an alignment cause this code?
faq.a: Many alignments require a steering angle sensor reset afterwards; skipping it sets a calibration code.
